body.x: Mippia, Inc. (CEO Chanho Oh) participated on Friday, December 12, in the “Global Media Meetup” hosted by AVING News’ International Press Club (IPC) for domestic companies and startups.

The Global Media Meetup focuses on introducing Korean companies' and startups' products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aims to proactively report on CES 2026 Innovation Award winners and CES-participating startups through global media channels and expand business opportunities.

Mippia is a Korean company founded to resolve recurring plagiarism and copyright infringement issues that arise unexpectedly during music production and creative processes. Backed by an organization with expertise spanning both music and AI engineering, the company operates a platform that enables musicians and entertainment companies worldwide to manage their intellectual property securely.

Specifically, Mippia provides integrated technologies for music IP protection, including AI-based music plagiarism checks, real-time plagiarism monitoring, and one-on-one music similarity analysis. Recognized for its functionality and high value, Mippia has rapidly secured domestic and global customers since its establishment in 2024 and has positioned itself as a worldwide service used by artists in 149 countries.

The platform, which shares its name with the company, supports differentiated musicological plagiarism detection using Mippia’s proprietary technology stack. Applying techniques published in SCIE-level academic papers, the system separates and extracts melody, rhythm, and harmony data from music tracks. It analyzes them using an ultra-fast AI clustering algorithm.

With this approach, the platform processes up to 100 million comparisons per track in under 1 minute and detects plagiarism even when tempo, key, instruments, or arrangements have changed. This enables responses to illegal remakes, remixes, sampling, and adaptations that other services cannot handle, while achieving up to 98% accuracy through advanced music analysis algorithms.

body.cap: Mippia CTO Seonghyeon Go presents at the Global Media Meetup held on Friday, December 12, at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Ease of use and intuitive operation also stand out as key strengths. The platform features a web-based, project-centered interface similar to creators’ existing workflows, allowing users to enter the analysis process immediately by simply uploading audio files on the relevant page.

The platform further visualizes the melody, rhythm, and harmony segments under analysis to offer more detailed comparison options. It generates analysis results in report layouts that even users without deep knowledge of DAWs or music theory can easily understand.

In addition, the system automatically detects data from millions of tracks released simultaneously worldwide. It can determine whether AI was involved in music production and, if so, the degree of AI involvement expressed as a percentage. The company explained that this enables effective and strategic responses to copyright confusion caused by the proliferation of AI-generated music and unauthorized distribution.

A Mippia official said, “As generative AI penetrates the creative domain, some forecasts suggest that losses in the global music industry could reach €1 billion by 2028,” adding, “Mippia contributes to identifying copyright responsibility through AI music registration and detection systems, while providing musicians and the industry with accurate data that serves as a basis for revenue.”

With its original and highly reliable plagiarism detection platform, Mippia was selected as a CES 2026 Innovation Award winner in the Enterprise Tech category. Leveraging this achievement, the company plans to accelerate its strategy to expand its customer base in major advanced markets and to pursue global partnerships to standardize its AI technology for copyright analysis and verification.

A company representative said, “To detect illegal distribution of music IP and build an automated copyright reporting system, we plan to pursue API integration with streaming platforms around the world,” and added, “Starting with CES, we will also participate in a series of overseas exhibitions in the music and AI fields, while working to secure strategic MOUs and proof-of-concept projects with entertainment companies in the United States, Japan, and Europe.”

Meanwhile, AVING News has introduced Korean companies to the world through partnership cooperation with more than 800 media outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building on its long-established global media network, AVING News launched the International Press Club in August. Media outlets participating in this Global Media Meetup included Innovation & Tech Today from the United States, Le Café Du Geek from France, Arageek from the United Arab Emirates, and Digitimes from Taiwan.
